mood.label: Cautiously bullish
mood.headline: Nifty closed near 23,000 on a 1.7% heavyweight rally, but weak breadth and Wipro's soft guidance cloud Friday.
mood.summary: Sensex jumped 1,533.72 points (+2.11%) to 74,315.61 and Nifty 374.65 points (+1.66%) to 22,997.35, the biggest gain since June, as cheaper crude (Brent ~$103.7), a fifth day of rupee gains (95.05) and buying in ICICI Bank, Reliance, Tech Mahindra and Bharti Airtel overrode a crash in Korea and Japan. The rally was narrow: smallcaps fell 1.31%, midcaps 0.36%, and declines beat advances 2,218 to 1,343 on NSE; Nestle (−7.8%) and Yes Bank (−14.5%) were the big losers. After the close Wipro guided Q3 revenue at −1.5% to +0.5% and its large-deal bookings fell 59%, and Persistent's profit fell 25%, so IT may cool on Friday. Nasdaq futures are down about 1.3%, and FIIs have sold for 14 straight days. Nifty needs to hold 22,800–22,844 to keep the breakout; 23,056–23,200 is the next hurdle, with Tech Mahindra's results and bonus due Friday and big bank results on Saturday.

brief.text: Nifty closed at 22,997.35 (+1.66%) and Sensex at 74,315.61 (+1,533.72 points), the biggest one-day gain since June, after touching 23,056 intraday.
ICICI Bank (+3.8%), Reliance (+3.4%), Tech Mahindra (+4.8%) and Bharti Airtel (+3.3%) led as Brent fell about 1.8% to near $104 and the rupee firmed to 95.05.
The gain was narrow: smallcaps fell 1.31%, 2,218 NSE stocks fell against 1,343 that rose, Nestle dropped 7.8% and Yes Bank 14.5% on the AT1 bond ruling.
After the close Wipro guided Q3 revenue at −1.5% to +0.5% and Persistent's profit fell 25%, so IT could give back some gains on Friday; BDL won a ₹1,307 cr Navy torpedo order.

Nifty must hold 22,800–22,844; resistance is 23,056–23,200. Tech Mahindra's results and bonus come Friday, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank and Yes Bank report Saturday, and markets shut Tuesday 20 Oct.

news.headline: Sensex surges 1,534 points, Nifty ends at 22,997 in best day since June
news.summary: Sensex closed at 74,315.61 (+2.11%) and Nifty at 22,997.35 (+1.66%) after touching 23,056. Cheaper crude, softer US bond yields and a firmer rupee drew buying into large caps, with money rotating out of crashing Asian tech markets.
news.why: Nifty is back above its 20-day average; holding 22,800 keeps the breakout alive into Saturday's bank results.

news.headline: Rally is narrow: smallcaps fall 1.3%, decliners beat advancers 2,218 to 1,343
news.summary: Nifty Smallcap 100 fell 1.31% and Midcap 100 0.36% while the benchmarks rallied. On NSE, 2,218 stocks fell and 1,343 rose; 83 hit 52-week lows against 69 at highs.
news.why: Gains concentrated in a few heavyweights usually fade faster; smaller holdings may not benefit from the index rally.

news.headline: Wipro guides Q3 revenue at −1.5% to +0.5%; large-deal bookings fall 59%
news.summary: Q2 profit fell 1.4% to ₹3,200.6 cr while revenue rose 9.1% to ₹24,750 cr. IT services revenue was flat in constant currency; total bookings fell 22.9% and large-deal bookings 58.6% from the June quarter. Operating margin was 16.5%.
news.why: The guidance points to no growth next quarter, which could cool Thursday's IT rally on Friday. Wipro closed +1.58% at ₹173.70 before the numbers.

news.headline: Persistent's profit falls 25% to ₹351.5 cr on Nagarro takeover costs
news.summary: Revenue rose to ₹4,663.9 cr from ₹3,580.7 cr, but profit fell from ₹471.5 cr as integration and financing costs of the 94% Nagarro SE purchase kicked in. It has given a corporate guarantee of up to €1,540 mn for bridge financing.
news.why: A profit fall is a negative surprise for a premium-valued IT stock; the reaction comes on Friday.

news.headline: Yes Bank crashes 14.5% after Supreme Court upholds quashing of ₹8,415 cr AT1 bond write-off
news.summary: The court upheld the Bombay High Court's 2023 order that the 2020 write-off of AT1 bonds was illegal. CRISIL had estimated a full write-back could cut the bank's core equity ratio by about 2.3–2.5 points. The stock hit a 20% lower limit at ₹16.96 and ended at ₹18.12 (Trendlyne).
news.why: The size of any payout is not yet clear; Yes Bank's Q2 results on Saturday 17 Oct should give the first disclosure.

news.headline: Nestle India sinks 7.8% despite 36% profit jump
news.summary: Q2 profit rose 36.3% to ₹1,026.7 cr and sales 20.5% to ₹6,782 cr, in line with estimates. The stock had gained about 6% in October; management flagged food inflation and cost pressure (Trendlyne), and it ended at ₹1,275.80, the top Nifty loser.
news.why: In-line results after a run-up get sold; the drop dragged FMCG and took 16.8 points off Nifty.

news.headline: Polycab slips 2% despite 53% revenue growth as margins narrow
news.summary: Revenue rose 53% to ₹9,898 cr and EBITDA 62%; profit rose to about ₹977–989 cr (sources differ). Trendlyne says the EBITDA margin fell 140 bps. NSE is also dropping it from F&O after the December series.
news.why: Strong growth is offset by margin and F&O-exit worries; the stock may stay volatile.

news.headline: Tata Communications jumps 5.5% as profit rises 86%
news.summary: Profit rose 86% to ₹341 cr and EBITDA 21% to ₹1,422 cr, with margin at 21.3%. Digital platform revenue grew 18.6% and digital losses halved. The stock touched ₹1,827.85 (+12.4%) and closed at ₹1,749.70 (Trendlyne).
news.why: A clear beat with improving margins; the stock gave back half its intraday jump, so dips may be better entries.

news.headline: Bharat Dynamics signs ₹1,307 cr Navy torpedo contract
news.summary: The contract for heavyweight torpedoes is worth about ₹1,307 cr plus taxes, to be delivered over 42 months. The order book was ₹26,176 cr at end-March. The stock closed at ₹1,126.30, roughly flat, before the news.
news.why: Announced after the close, so it is not in the price yet; the long delivery period means revenue comes gradually.

news.headline: IDBI Bank slides 8% a day after Cabinet clears Fairfax sale
news.summary: IDBI fell 8.1% to ₹83.07, close to Fairfax's ₹81 deal price, after a 9% jump on Wednesday. Fairfax reportedly plans to combine IDBI Bank, Digit Insurance and IIFL Capital into one group.
news.why: With the share now near the deal price, the open-offer terms for public shareholders matter most.

news.headline: Goyal: first tranche of India–US trade deal finalised, now in legal drafting
news.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the first tranche has been finalised and is being legally drafted, and that India will operationalise it once it gets an edge over peer countries. US Ambassador Sergio Gor said the two sides are very close (Bloomberg).
news.why: A signed deal would help US-focused exporters such as textiles, gems and jewellery, auto parts and chemicals; no tariff details yet.

news.headline: Rupee gains for fifth day, closes at 95.05
news.summary: The rupee rose 12 paise to 95.05 a dollar, 183 paise stronger over five sessions, helped by cheaper oil, unwinding of dollar bets and RBI support. A wider trade deficit and importer demand capped gains.
news.why: A firmer rupee eases imported inflation and FII currency losses, but trims rupee gold prices.

news.headline: Brent eases toward $104 as US weighs easing sanctions on Gulf crude
news.summary: Brent December futures were near $103.70 and WTI near $94.71 by 3:35 PM IST, off nearly $106 earlier in the week, on reports the US may ease sanctions on West Asian crude shipping. The Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted.
news.why: Every dollar off crude helps India's import bill, the rupee and oil marketing companies; HPCL rose 5.3%.

news.headline: Kospi sinks 7.7%, Nikkei 4.8% as AI tech rout deepens; Nasdaq futures down 1.3%
news.summary: Samsung fell 9.5% and SK Hynix 11.4% as hot US inflation and AI-funding worries hit chip stocks. Nasdaq 100 futures were down 1.26% early in US hours, while Dow futures rose. Europe's tech sector fell 3.2%.
news.why: India gained as a rotation destination today, but another bad US tech session could weigh on Indian IT on Friday.

news.headline: Fed hike odds swing back below 30%; US yields at three-week low
news.summary: Odds of a Fed hike on 28 Oct briefly topped 50% after Wednesday's CPI, then fell below 30%. The US 10-year yield slipped to about 5.08–5.11%. US producer prices and retail sales are due tonight.
news.why: Softer US yields are what drew money into Indian large caps today; hot PPI data tonight could reverse that.

news.headline: Other Q2s: HDFC AMC +5.1%, Indian Bank profit +15%, IRFC +10% with ₹1.15 dividend
news.summary: HDFC AMC's profit rose about 4% to ₹749 cr on 14% revenue growth and the stock gained 5.1%. Indian Bank's profit rose 15% to ₹3,462 cr with gross NPA at 1.61%, but the share fell 1.7%. IRFC's profit rose 10% to ₹1,958 cr; record date for its ₹1.15 dividend is 23 Oct. HDFC Life's H1 value of new business rose 12% with a 24.7% margin.
news.why: Steady numbers; HDFC AMC's jump shows markets rewarding capital-market plays.

news.headline: NTPC seeks ₹1.5 lakh cr Rosatom tie-up for six nuclear reactors
news.summary: NTPC is exploring large nuclear reactor projects with Russia's Rosatom, and France's EDF, with an estimated ₹1.5 lakh cr outlay for six reactors. It is a proposal, not a signed deal.
news.why: Supports the long-term nuclear theme (BHEL, L&T), but capex this size takes years and needs government approval.

news.headline: Friday: Tech Mahindra results and bonus; LTM, Federal Bank, Bajaj Housing report; big banks Saturday
news.summary: Tech Mahindra's board meets 15–16 Oct on results, a bonus issue and an interim dividend. LTM, Federal Bank, Bajaj Housing Finance, Oberoi Realty, Urban Company and Crompton report Friday; HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank and Yes Bank on Saturday 17 Oct.
news.why: Bank results on a Saturday mean Monday's open can gap either way; Tuesday 20 Oct is a market holiday.

gold.label: Firm; rupee trims
gold.summary: World gold rose about 1% to roughly $4,135–4,160 as US yields fell to a three-week low and the dollar index slipped 0.57% to 101.96 after Wednesday's CPI spike reversed. MCX December gold was ₹1,47,850 per 10g (+1.37%) at 3:37 PM, so gold ETFs like GOLDBEES should be firmer, though the rupee's fifth daily gain to 95.05 trims part of the move. MCX range to watch: ₹1,46,400–1,48,605; US PPI tonight and the 28 Oct Fed meeting are the main risks.
gold.how: Indian gold ETFs track the domestic gold rate: world gold in dollars × USD/INR, plus import duty. So both world events and the rupee move them.

scenarios.title: Dollar keeps sliding
scenarios.why: The dollar fully reversed its post-CPI spike and the US 10-year yield fell to about 5.1%. If that continues, world gold gains; a firmer rupee takes back a small part for Indian ETFs.
scenarios.when: DXY 101.96 (−0.57%) on 15 Oct; US PPI and retail sales tonight
scenarios.line: DXY −0.6% and US yields at a 3-week low lifted gold ~1%.

scenarios.title: Fed holds on 28 Oct (~70% odds)
scenarios.why: Hike odds briefly topped 50% after Wednesday's CPI, then fell below 30% (Saxo). A clear pause would pull yields and the dollar down, which gold needs to get back above $4,235. The rupee may firm a little, trimming part of the gain in India.
scenarios.line: Yields and dollar ease; gold's best chance to clear $4,235.

scenarios.title: Fed hikes on 28 Oct (<30% odds)
scenarios.why: Hot September CPI (3.7%) briefly made a hike a coin-flip before odds fell back. A hike would push the dollar and US yields higher and could send gold back toward the $4,066 low. FII selling in India would likely rise too, weakening the rupee and cushioning part of the fall.
scenarios.line: Odds swung above 50% and back under 30%; gold toward $4,066.

scenarios.title: Gulf conflict widens, oil spikes
scenarios.why: Gold usually jumps on war fears, and higher oil weakens the rupee, so Indian gold ETFs gain on both counts. The catch: costly oil also feeds inflation and Fed-hike fears, which has capped gold's rallies recently, so gains can fade.
scenarios.when: Brent ~$103.7–104 (15 Oct); Hormuz still disrupted; US weighing easing tanker sanctions
scenarios.line: Safe-haven buying plus a weaker rupee; can fade on inflation fears.

scenarios.title: US–Iran de-escalation
scenarios.why: Less war risk removes some safe-haven buying, though cheaper oil also lowers inflation and hike fears, which helps gold. The clearer effect for India is a stronger rupee, which pulls the rupee price of gold down.
scenarios.when: Reports on 15 Oct that the US may ease sanctions on West Asian crude shipping; no talks scheduled
scenarios.line: Less haven demand and a stronger rupee pull Indian gold down.

scenarios.title: Rupee slides past 97
scenarios.why: Every 1% fall in the rupee adds roughly 1% to Indian gold ETF prices even if world gold is flat. FII selling (14 straight days) and Brent above $100 are the pressures, but the rupee has gained five days in a row on RBI's steps and cheaper oil.
scenarios.when: USD/INR vs 97 (record low 96.96); now 95.05 close; daily FII flows; Brent
scenarios.line: Each 1% rupee fall adds ~1% to gold ETFs, even with gold flat.

scenarios.title: Rupee recovers
scenarios.why: The rupee has gained 183 paise in five sessions (to 95.05) on RBI support, cheaper oil and unwinding of dollar bets, a big reason MCX gold has lagged world gold. A further 2% recovery would knock about 2% off Indian gold ETFs.
scenarios.when: USD/INR 95.05 close on 15 Oct; support 94.70, resistance 95.50 (HDFC Securities)
scenarios.line: Rupee up ~1.9% in 5 days; another 2% would cut ~2% off gold ETFs.

scenarios.title: Stock market sell-off
scenarios.why: Investors move money into gold when stocks fall. The WGC says weak Indian equities drove gold ETF buying in September. In a severe crash gold can dip briefly as people sell everything to raise cash, then recover.
scenarios.when: Nifty 22,997 (+1.66%) but smallcaps −1.31%; Kospi −7.7%, Nikkei −4.8%; India VIX ~14
scenarios.line: Money shifts to gold when stocks fall; Asian tech crash is the live risk.

scenarios.title: Central banks keep buying
scenarios.why: China's central bank added 21 tonnes in September, its 23rd straight monthly purchase. Steady official buying tends to limit how far gold falls, though it rarely drives short-term moves.
scenarios.line: China added 21 t in Sept (23rd month); limits downside.

scenarios.title: India cuts import duty
scenarios.why: Indian gold ETFs track the domestic price, which includes customs duty. A duty cut would lower the Indian gold price, and ETF prices, overnight by about the size of the cut, as happened in the July 2024 Budget. A duty hike would do the opposite.
scenarios.line: Domestic gold, and ETFs, drop overnight by about the cut.

guide._all: Each card is a company-specific event from the latest filings and news. Green = likely to support the share, red = likely to pressure it, amber = watch. Tap a type to see what usually happens next. New after the close: BDL's ₹1,307 cr Navy torpedo order (positive, not yet in the price), and weak numbers from Wipro (soft Q3 guidance) and Persistent (profit −25%). Yes Bank fell 14.5% on the AT1 bond ruling and Nestle 7.8% after results; HDB Financial turned negative at a record low. No client-loss or order-cancellation news found today. Review-by dates are counted in trading days (20 Oct is a market holiday).
guide.Can rise: Positive triggers. A share does not always rise on good news, especially if it ran up before the announcement or the overall market is weak.
guide.Can fall: Negative triggers. Results misses, big investor exits and weak business updates usually hit the share on the day and can weigh for weeks.
guide.Order won: An order matters most when it is big compared with the company's yearly revenue (5–10% or more is significant for smaller companies). Repeat orders and orders in a new area are good signs of future growth. Check the execution period: a 24-month order adds revenue slowly. Being named the only qualified bidder (Goodluck) is a step before an order, not an order itself.
guide.Results: Shares react to results versus expectations, not just growth. Profit growing slower than sales signals squeezed margins, in-line results after a run-up often get sold (Nestle), and guidance for the next quarter can matter more than the quarter itself (Wipro). The earnings call commentary often matters as much as the numbers.
guide.Business update: Monthly sales, pre-sales and festive data give an early read on the quarter before results come out.
guide.Board decision: Board outcomes that usually lift a share: buyback, bonus, stock split, special dividend, demerger or merger that simplifies the group. Ones that can pressure it: big equity fund raise (QIP or rights issue) that adds new shares, large acquisitions that need fresh capital (Aegis), or large related-party deals.
guide.Stake sale: When a promoter or big investor sells in a block deal, the share often falls on the day because the sale is at a discount. If quality institutions buy, it usually recovers within weeks.
guide.Regulatory: For pharma: a USFDA warning letter or import alert is a big negative, while a Form 483 with a few procedural observations (Dr Reddy's) is usually minor. Approvals, certifications and cuts in tax demands (Paytm) are positives; new or higher tax demands (Mphasis) and lawsuits (Bank of Baroda) are negatives, though most are disputed for years. Rule changes by NPCI, SEBI or the exchanges (UPI fees, F&O exits) can move a whole group of stocks.
guide.Management change: A sudden exit of a CEO or CFO can spook investors; a planned succession usually doesn't.
guide.Corporate action: Takeovers, open offers and delisting plans. These change who owns the company and can create short-term price moves. If the share already trades above the deal price (IDBI Bank), the upside depends on the open-offer terms.
guide.Fund raise: Debt or government loans don't dilute shareholders. Equity raises (QIP, rights, preferential issue) add new shares and can weigh on the price.
guide.Legal claim: A lawsuit or legal claim against a company. A big headline number can hit the share for days, but most claims take years and are often dismissed or settled for far less. Watch whether the court admits the case and what the company files.

items.title: India–US trade deal
items.who: Commerce Ministry and US Trade Representative
items.latest: On 15 Oct Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the first tranche of the deal has been finalised and is in legal drafting, and India will operationalise it once it gets a competitive edge over peer countries. US Ambassador Sergio Gor said the two sides are very close (Bloomberg). No tariff details have been released.
items.effect: A deal that lowers US tariffs would help exporters that depend on the US: textiles and apparel, gems and jewellery, auto parts, chemicals, seafood. Failure or new tariffs would hit the same group.
items.when: First tranche: legal drafting under way; signing date not fixed
items.likely: Medium to high: first tranche finalised per the minister, but not yet signed
items.watch: Signing date and tariff details for textiles, gems, auto parts and chemicals

items.title: US Federal Reserve rate decision
items.latest: After Wednesday's hot September CPI (3.7%), odds of a 28 Oct hike briefly topped 50%, then fell back below 30% (Saxo). SF Fed's Mary Daly said more hikes are likely needed but there is no urgency this month. The US 10-year yield eased to about 5.08–5.11%.
items.effect: A hold is mildly positive for Indian stocks, the rupee and gold. A surprise hike would lift the dollar and US yields, push FIIs to sell more, and hurt IT and gold.
items.likely: Hold more likely (~70%) in October; hike risk by December
items.watch: US PPI and retail sales (15 Oct), jobs data

items.title: RBI rate decision: another hike likely in December
items.latest: RBI hiked the repo rate to 5.50% on 7 Oct. September CPI came in at 5.54% (above the 5.4% forecast). HDFC Bank, DBS, Oxford Economics and others now expect 25 bps more in December; some see 50–75 bps more this year.
items.effect: A hike raises borrowing costs: negative for rate-sensitive stocks such as NBFCs, real estate and autos, and for bond prices. Banks can gain on margins at first. A pause would be a relief rally trigger.
items.likely: High for a 25 bps hike, based on economist forecasts

items.title: IDBI Bank sold to Fairfax (60.72% stake at ₹81/share)
items.latest: On 14 Oct the Cabinet approved Fairfax's ₹52,878 cr bid: the government sells 30.48% and LIC 30.24% at ₹81 a share. IDBI jumped 9% to ₹90.39 on 14 Oct, then fell 8.1% to ₹83.07 on 15 Oct. Fairfax reportedly plans to combine IDBI Bank, Digit Insurance and IIFL Capital into one group.
items.effect: Largest privatisation since Air India and a boost to reform sentiment. For IDBI shareholders, the stock already trades above ₹81; open-offer terms for public shareholders are not yet announced, so chasing the jump is risky. Fairfax must merge or exit CSB Bank, where it owns 40%.
items.likely: High (approved); RBI fit-and-proper and CCI clearances still needed
items.watch: Open-offer price and size; RBI approval; government's plan to sell its remaining 15%

items.title: Scrap LTCG tax on shares (and possibly cut STT)
items.who: Proposed by SBI Research · Decision: Finance Ministry
items.latest: SBI Research (12 Oct) proposed scrapping long-term capital gains tax on equities, with a 2–3 year holding period, to stem FPI outflows of ₹3.04 lakh cr this year. On 14 Oct the Finance Minister said it is 'too early to comment' and announced no change.
items.effect: If done, a big positive for the whole market and for FPI flows; brokers, exchanges and AMCs would gain most. Current LTCG is 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh. A cut in STT on F&O (raised to 0.05% on futures in April) would mainly help brokers and BSE.
items.likely: Low to medium: equity LTCG brought in about ₹1.29 lakh cr, hard to give up with a ~4.5% fiscal deficit
items.watch: Pre-Budget consultations (Nov–Jan) and any Finance Ministry comment

items.title: SEBI closing auction for the final price
items.latest: SEBI received 3,500+ comments on a Closing Auction Session to set closing prices more fairly. On 10 Oct Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said guidelines on expiry-day settlement prices should come in about a week, with changes targeted by end-November. Investor-awareness messages on broker apps start 1 Nov.
items.effect: Changes how the closing price is set at 3:30 PM. Mainly affects traders and index funds; little effect on long-term holders. Exchanges and brokers may need system changes.
items.when: Guidelines expected within days; changes targeted by end-November

items.title: 0.4% UPI merchant fee on payments above ₹2,000
items.latest: On 13 Oct NPCI deferred the 0.4% merchant discount rate on certain UPI merchant payments above ₹2,000 until after Diwali; a new date will be notified.
items.effect: A fee on large UPI merchant payments would give payment companies a revenue source; small merchants would bear the cost. Positive for payment firms such as Paytm when it starts.
items.when: After Diwali (8 Nov); new date to be notified
items.watch: NPCI circular with the start date

items.title: US midterm elections and Iran risk
items.latest: Midterms are on 3 Nov. President Trump said there will be no US strike on Iran before then. The Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted, but on 15 Oct reports said the US is weighing easing sanctions on West Asian crude shipping, pulling Brent toward $104.
items.effect: After 3 Nov the Iran pledge expires, so oil and safe-haven risk could rise. Higher oil hurts India (rupee, inflation, oil marketing companies, paints, airlines) and helps gold and upstream oil.

items.title: OPEC+ oil output for December
items.latest: On 4–5 Oct OPEC+ kept November output unchanged. The next monthly decision (for December) is due in early November.
items.effect: Higher output would ease crude and help India's rupee, inflation and oil marketing companies. A cut would do the opposite.
items.watch: Brent near $103.7–104 (15 Oct); US sanctions easing on tankers

items.title: More PSU stake sales (OFS) this year
items.latest: About ₹55,757 cr raised so far in FY27 from stake sales in 9 PSUs (including LIC and Coal India). With IDBI, receipts cross the ₹80,000 cr target for the first time in 8 years. The government may sell its residual IDBI stake in the market.
items.effect: An offer-for-sale (OFS) is usually priced at a discount, so the PSU stock often dips for a few days around the sale. Meeting the target can reduce pressure for further big sales this year.
items.when: Through March 2027; OFS dates are announced a day ahead
items.watch: OFS announcements on NSE/BSE (usually the evening before)

items.title: GST process reforms
items.latest: The GST Council approved process reforms at its 8 Oct meeting to speed decisions and cut compliance; the Prime Minister welcomed them. Details of each change are still being notified.
items.effect: Lower compliance cost helps small businesses and consumer companies over time; no immediate rate change.

items.title: Union Budget 2027
items.latest: Preparations are under way. The LTCG/STT debate, disinvestment, capex and the fiscal deficit (~4.5% of GDP) will be the key themes.
items.effect: Tax changes on capital gains or STT, customs duty on gold, and capex plans can move whole sectors on the day.
items.watch: Pre-Budget meetings and leaks from December
